title: Do Diverse Copies Hold a Mission Deeper Than Cloned Copies When Failures Share a Cause?

e1.name: Correlated-copy depth simulator
e1.note: Identical copies share a common-cause channel; adding clones past a few barely lifts survival when β>0. Diverse classes keep stacking.

e2.name: Backblaze same-model co-failure β
e2.source: Backblaze Hard Drive Stats, 2019 Q1 and Q2 daily snapshots (public)
e2.note: β̂ is the share of same-model window pairs above an exposure-aware independent null — a lower bound on common-cause clustering, not a claim about agent fleets.

e3.name: Plug measured β into depth model
e3.note: Structural plug-in only. Backblaze β is storage hardware; the depth model is an Infinite Octaves nesting analogy, not a live multi-agent bake-off.

e4.name: Yeast paralog buffering (SGD null inviable)
e4.source: SGD phenotype_data.tab (null mutants) and SGD_features.tab; Ensembl BioMart paralogues for S. cerevisiae
e4.note: Public SGD null phenotypes + Ensembl yeast paralogs. Soft Story for agent fleets: a second diverged copy buffers single-copy loss more than a near-clone does.

e5.name: Human paralog × gnomAD LOEUF
e5.source: gnomAD v2.1.1 constraint by gene (LOEUF = oe_lof_upper; genes with expected LoF >= 10); Ensembl BioMart human paralogues
e5.note: gnomAD constraint + Ensembl human paralogs. Soft Story only — not clinical genetics, not a claim that LOEUF proves agent-fleet diversity.

verdict: Positive expedition signal on E1, E2, E3, E4, E5: cloned copies share failure modes under common-cause β while diverse classes keep nesting depth; public yeast/human paralog boards and Backblaze same-model clustering support the rhyme.
